hints: Notice that waiting less than 10 minutes includes waiting less than 5 minutes as well as waiting between 5 and 10 minutes.
Subtract $\mathrm{P}(T < 5) = 0.16$ from $\mathrm{P}(T < 10) = 0.88$ to find the probability of the interval between 5 and 10 minutes.
walkthrough:
Express the probability of waiting between 5 and 10 minutes as the difference between the two cumulative probabilities:
$$\mathrm{P}(5 \le T < 10) = \mathrm{P}(T < 10) - \mathrm{P}(T < 5)$$

Substitute the given numerical probabilities:
$$\mathrm{P}(5 \le T < 10) = 0.88 - 0.16 = 0.72$$

ai_rubric.Applying the Addition Rule: Combines the relevant mutually exclusive probabilities without double-counting.

teacher_walkthrough:
Let $T$ represent the waiting time at the dentist in minutes. We are given two cumulative probabilities:
$$\mathrm{P}(T < 5) = 0.16 \quad \text{and} \quad \mathrm{P}(T < 10) = 0.88$$

The interval of waiting less than 10 minutes is composed of two mutually exclusive events:
1. Waiting less than 5 minutes ($T < 5$)
2. Waiting between 5 and 10 minutes ($5 \le T < 10$)
Therefore, by the addition rule for mutually exclusive events:
$$\mathrm{P}(T < 10) = \mathrm{P}(T < 5) + \mathrm{P}(5 \le T < 10)$$

Rearrange to isolate $\mathrm{P}(5 \le T < 10)$ by subtracting $\mathrm{P}(T < 5)$ from both sides:
$$\mathrm{P}(5 \le T < 10) = \mathrm{P}(T < 10) - \mathrm{P}(T < 5)$$
Substitute the values:
$$\mathrm{P}(5 \le T < 10) = 0.88 - 0.16 = 0.72$$

hints: Model the number of people who wait between 5 and 10 minutes as a binomial distribution $X \sim \mathrm{B}(n, p)$ with $n = 180$ and $p = 0.72$ from part (i).
Calculate the parameters for the approximating normal distribution: mean $\mu = np$ and variance $\sigma^2 = np(1 - p)$.
Apply a continuity correction to the strict discrete inequality $X > 115$: in the continuous model, this corresponds to $\mathrm{P}(Y > 115.5)$.
Standardise $115.5$ using $Z = \dfrac{115.5 - \mu}{\sigma}$, and evaluate the normal tail probability using symmetry $\mathrm{P}(Z > -z) = \Phi(z)$.
walkthrough:
Define the binomial variable $X \sim \mathrm{B}(180, 0.72)$ and calculate the normal approximation parameters for $Y \sim \mathrm{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$:
$$\mu = np = 180 \times 0.72 = 129.6$$
$$\sigma^2 = np(1 - p) = 180 \times 0.72 \times 0.28 = 36.288$$
$$\sigma = \sqrt{36.288} \approx 6.02395$$

Apply the continuity correction to the inequality $X > 115$, which corresponds to $X \ge 116$ in discrete integers:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 115) \approx \mathrm{P}(Y > 115.5)$$

Evaluate the probability using standard normal distribution tables:
$$\mathrm{P}(Z > -2.341) = \Phi(2.341) \approx 0.9903 \approx 0.990$$

ai_rubric.Applying a Normal Approximation: Uses the binomial mean and variance for the normal approximation.
ai_rubric.Applying a Continuity Correction: Moves the discrete boundary by one half before standardising.

teacher_walkthrough:
Let $X$ denote the number of people out of the sample of 180 who wait between 5 and 10 minutes. Because trials are independent with constant probability $p = 0.72$, $X$ follows a binomial distribution:
$$X \sim \mathrm{B}(180, 0.72)$$

Since $n = 180$ is large and both $np = 129.6 > 5$ and $n(1-p) = 50.4 > 5$, we can approximate $X$ using a normal distribution $Y \sim \mathrm{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$. Calculate the mean:
$$\mu = n p = 180 \times 0.72 = 129.6$$
Calculate the variance:
$$\sigma^2 = n p (1 - p) = 180 \times 0.72 \times (1 - 0.72) = 180 \times 0.72 \times 0.28$$
Multiply the terms:
$$180 \times 0.72 = 129.6$$
$$129.6 \times 0.28 = 36.288$$
The standard deviation is:
$$\sigma = \sqrt{36.288} \approx 6.02395$$

Next, apply the continuity correction. In a discrete distribution, 'more than 115' means $X \in \{116, 117, 118, \dots\}$. The discrete bar for 116 begins at $115.5$ on a continuous scale, so:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 115) = \mathrm{P}(X \ge 116) \approx \mathrm{P}(Y > 115.5)$$

Now standardise $Y = 115.5$ using the standard normal score formula:
$$Z = \frac{Y - \mu}{\sigma}$$
Substitute $Y = 115.5$, $\mu = 129.6$, and $\sigma = \sqrt{36.288}$:
$$Z = \frac{115.5 - 129.6}{\sqrt{36.288}}$$
Subtract in the numerator:
$$115.5 - 129.6 = -14.1$$
Divide by the standard deviation:
$$Z = \frac{-14.1}{6.02395} \approx -2.34066 \approx -2.341$$

We need to find $\mathrm{P}(Z > -2.341)$. By the symmetry of the normal distribution, the area to the right of $-2.341$ equals the area to the left of $+2.341$:
$$\mathrm{P}(Z > -2.341) = \mathrm{P}(Z < 2.341) = \Phi(2.341)$$
Look up $2.341$ in the standard normal tables:
$$\Phi(2.34) = 0.9904, \quad \text{difference for } 1 = -0.0001 \implies \Phi(2.341) = 0.9903$$
Round to 3 significant figures:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 115) \approx 0.990$$
